title: Observe, review, or send the daily enacted-decision digest
summary: Continuously classify explicit user settlements from completed effectful root Codex turns, inspect durable verdicts and candidates, project the previous local day, or send its frozen digest through Email.
use_when: Post-activation enacted decisions across local Codex tasks should be observed or summarized.
Observer coverage, a decision candidate, or its review state should be inspected.
A terminal observation failure should be deliberately requeued after its cause is diagnosed and corrected.
One previously observer-deferred Stop-hook source has been proven permanently unavailable and should be explicitly closed as not eligible.
The user explicitly requests a manual decision-digest email send.
do_not_use_when: A raw conversation lookup or full-text search is the intended outcome.
The intended decision has no same-turn completed file change and therefore falls outside this enacted projection.
A file write, plan, recommendation, question, status report, or assistant-only conclusion should be treated as decision authority.
The source is merely unfinished, or any source or classification state has already been bound.
External sending has not been authorized and no installed recurring authorization applies.
outcome: Durable per-authority enacted-decision coverage, one audited unavailable-source closure, a daily projection complete as of its recorded turn-completion cutoff, a local frozen preview, one review event, or one idempotent Email submission.
effects: The synchronous Stop hook durably upserts only a session/turn correlation and performs no model work.

One observer worker resolves a completed root turn through Conversations and may submit bounded serial Nucleus classification over all eligible current-turn authorities, the immediately preceding assistant proposal needed to interpret them when one exists, and at most the final assistant result; prior normalized context is added only after a validated needs-context result.

Daily build records a durable completion cutoff, reconciles and drains to a fixed point, captures a SQLite-rowid observation-admission watermark, and projects only post-baseline observations completed by the cutoff and admitted through that watermark; the normal 09:00 path performs no model work, while exceptional catch-up may invoke Nucleus.
An explicitly authorized observation retry increments that failed observation's attempt epoch and retains its prior jobs and receipts.

An explicitly confirmed unavailable-source abandonment waits for the serial observer lock and changes only a previously pending, entirely unbound queued correlation to complete and not eligible with a fixed audit marker.
Review changes durable candidate state and invalidates the prior digest revision.
Send discloses normalized decision statements and IDs to Email, Resend, and the fixed recipient provider.
authority: Only an explicit user settlement in an eligible completed root turn is decision authority; a completed file change selects scope but cannot authorize meaning.
Only explicit recovery authorization after source diagnosis can authorize unavailable-source abandonment; source absence and model output cannot.
The Decisions SQLite database owns activation baseline, observation verdicts, candidates, projection, review, snapshot, and delivery state.
Nucleus owns agent execution but not decision truth or digest success.
Email owns Resend submission; the recipient provider owns receipt.
success: A classified observation succeeds only after unique turn resolution, post-baseline authority, at least one completed nonempty fileChange, one validated decision or no-decision verdict per supplied user message, and the observation transaction complete.

Unavailable-source abandonment succeeds only for a previously observer-deferred pending level-0 row with a retry time but no not-completed marker, bound source, job, authority, verdict, or candidate; it records complete/not-eligible plus conversation_source_abandoned.

Daily build succeeds only after complete reconciliation and terminal observation coverage for eligible turns completed by its durable cutoff in the exact post-baseline report window; any failed or unresolved observation known by that cutoff blocks normal and all-clear delivery.
Preview exactly reports one frozen projection revision without network access.
Send reports the Email message ID persisted under the frozen delivery key.
failure_and_recovery: Processing, reconciliation, and projection require the write-once observer baseline; default activation stores the next whole Unix second, pre-baseline and cutover-second authority is never backfilled, and redeploy never advances the baseline.

The Stop hook is synchronous and idempotent so accepted ingest is durable before turn completion; a missed or untrusted hook is recovered by content-free reconciliation, which enqueues but never classifies.

Observe process resumes one processing observation first, skips queued observations before their retry time, and orders ready queued work by retry-ready time so a deferred source yields without creating parallel workers.

Only a positively observed terminal failure permits retry1 and retry2 within a scope. A terminally failed observation is not automatically requeued and blocks its daily projection; explicit observe retry is a separate recovery action after correction and preserves prior audit history.

Observe abandon requires --source-unavailable and proven permanent source unavailability, never a merely unfinished turn; it is idempotent only for the exact prior abandonment, stores no free-form reason, creates no verdict, candidate, or lifecycle event, and leaves the baseline unchanged.
Completed-root reconciliation fails closed if a source explicitly abandoned as unavailable later appears.
The single allowed needs-context transition requeues the same observation with prior normalized conversation context; it does not widen decision authority beyond the original turn.

A turn completing after a projection's cutoff can enter a later manual rebuild of its authority date, but an accepted scheduled delivery is not automatically amended and the late turn is not carried into another date.
Legacy interrupted scan runs retain their original retry and explicit daily-abandon recovery; that legacy daily abandonment never mutates continuous observations.
A repeated scheduled occurrence reuses the same frozen body and idempotency key.
A manual retry for the same run revision reuses a pending or failed ad-hoc key; a new key is created only after acceptance, and manual delivery never consumes scheduled state.
privacy: Hook ingest persists only session and turn correlation; it discards transcript path, working directory, model, permission mode, latest assistant message, and other event fields.

The level-0 classifier receives all eligible current-turn user authorities, the immediately preceding assistant proposal needed to interpret them when one exists, at most the final assistant result, and only a completed-file-change count—never the whole turn/thread, paths, diffs, commands, reasoning, approvals, or tool output; prior message context is sent only for the single validated expansion.

Nucleus durably retains each exact classifier request prompt and tool exchange in its private local database without automatic pruning: the bounded level-0 slice initially, or the normalized full thread prefix after level-1 expansion. Nucleus owns retention and recovery of those records.
Conversation text is not copied into the Decisions database; only request digests, source anchors, verdicts, normalized candidates, and text-free validated receipt DTOs are retained.
Unavailable-source abandonment retains only a fixed product-owned marker and detail, never caller-provided text.
Email statements pass deterministic fail-closed disclosure checks and exclude raw transcript excerpts, rationales, credentials, account/email identifiers, source IDs, tool output, and local paths.
Observer and scheduled runners use scrubbed environments, body-free logs, and never store or forward Email credentials.
does_not_authorize: Sending when only observation, reconciliation, build, preview, inspection, or review was requested.
Changing the Email recipient, sender, or Resend account.
Abandoning a source without explicit recovery authorization, before permanent unavailability is proven, or after any source or classification state has been bound.
Resetting the observer baseline, requeuing a terminal failure without explicit recovery authority, or treating model output, file activity, or delivery acceptance as source truth.

consumers.statement: The current user may inspect continuous enacted-decision coverage, review candidates, build and preview one local-day projection, explicitly repair eligible failures, or authorize an immediate digest send; the installed daily service may use only its separately established recurring send authority.
Raw-conversation readers, decisions without a same-turn completed file change, arbitrary email recipients, and downstream lifecycle consumers are not served through this digest capability.

preconditions.statement: Continuous processing and projection require the write-once observer baseline, a uniquely resolved completed root turn, post-baseline user authority, and at least one successfully completed nonempty fileChange in the same turn.

Classification requires compatible Conversations source resolution and Nucleus execution; sending additionally requires an exact frozen snapshot, explicit or installed standing send authority, and compatible Email transport.

Retry requires a diagnosed and corrected terminal observation failure, while source abandonment requires explicit recovery authorization and proof that one previously deferred entirely unbound source is permanently unavailable.

inputs.statement: Supported commands accept an optional exact local calendar date, an exact decision ID for review or inspection, or an exact observation ID for retry or guarded source-unavailable abandonment.

The observer consumes only normalized completed-turn evidence from Conversations: eligible user authorities, minimal proposal and final-response context, content-free file-change count, and at most one validated prior-context expansion.
Paths, diffs, commands, reasoning, approvals, tool output, raw transcript files, caller-authored abandonment reasons, and user-supplied email addresses are not accepted as digest authority inputs.

outputs.statement: Observation produces durable per-authority decision or no-decision coverage, or one narrowly audited no-verdict source-unavailable closure; inspection returns durable candidate and observer state.

Build produces a cutoff- and admission-watermark-bounded daily run, preview freezes and renders one exact run revision locally, review appends a state transition, and send persists one Email acceptance identifier under its delivery key.
The capability returns no raw transcript export, Gmail-receipt proof, unbounded historical digest, automatic amendment of an accepted send, or authority inferred from file activity or model prose.

data_semantics.statement: An enacted decision is an explicit user settlement in a completed root turn made eligible by a same-turn completed nonempty file change; the effect selects scope but never supplies decision meaning.

A no-decision verdict is durable negative coverage, a complete/not-eligible source abandonment is audited absence of classifiable source rather than a verdict, and Nucleus completion is execution evidence rather than Decisions truth.
A daily projection is complete only as of its durable turn-completion cutoff and observation-admission watermark; Email acceptance proves submission, not Gmail delivery.

identity_and_units.statement: Decision ID derives from host, canonical authority item, and exact byte span; observation, run, revision, candidate, review, Nucleus job, delivery, and external message IDs identify separate records.

Report dates are machine-local calendar days, authority and completion times preserve their documented precision, the activation baseline is an absolute instant, and SQLite append position or rowid—not timestamps—orders lifecycle and admission frontiers.
The digest publishes no usage, cost, or billing unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: A successful observation covers every eligible user authority supplied for its one completed turn with exactly one validated decision or no-decision verdict, except the separately audited source-unavailable state which binds no authority.

A successful daily build reaches a fixed point and includes all post-baseline eligible turns completed by its cutoff and observations admitted through its fixed watermark; any known unresolved or failed item blocks normal and all-clear delivery.
A later-completing turn may enter a later manual rebuild of its authority date but never another date and never automatically amends an already accepted scheduled delivery.
No wall-clock bound from turn completion to observation, projection, review, Email acceptance, or Gmail receipt is promised, and no perpetual retention horizon is declared here.

access.statement: Supported access is through the current-user Decisions CLI, its exact user Stop hook, and its two installed local LaunchAgent runners; direct SQLite mutation is unsupported.
Only an explicit current request or separately installed recurring authority permits sending, and source abandonment has its own explicit recovery authorization and fail-closed state guard.
Observation, reconciliation, build, preview, review, catalog discovery, or possession of an Email key does not authorize disclosure or sending.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Stop ingest idempotently records only correlation, one serial worker resumes processing first and otherwise selects ready queued work by retry time, and at most one validated context expansion occurs before transactional verdict and candidate commit.

A terminal failure remains blocking until explicitly retried with a new attempt epoch; guarded source abandonment is serialized, changes only one still-unbound pending row, is idempotent for the exact success, and makes later source discovery fail closed.
Review and lifecycle history append atomically, snapshot bodies freeze by run revision, and duplicate scheduled or unresolved manual delivery uses the same stable idempotency key and exact body.

operational_limits.statement: Observation processing is serial, source context expands at most once, each scope has one initial Nucleus attempt plus at most two retries after positively observed terminal failure, and the scheduled service runs at local 09:00.

The capability stops on incomplete or ambiguous source, missing baseline, failed or unresolved coverage, invalid classifier output, incompatible dependencies, unproven permanent source absence, or unauthorized sending.
It provides no parallel whole-history classification, arbitrary queue clearing, implicit source abandonment, pre-baseline backfill, recipient configuration, or direct-Codex fallback.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Provider release, capability contract version, Decisions SQLite schema, immutable classification schema and toolset, lifecycle envelope, Email contract, Conversations contract, and Nucleus protocol remain distinct compatibility axes.
Legacy schema-version-one runs and receipts remain readable, migrations are explicit, and changed registered meaning uses a new immutable identity with historical decoding retained.
No universal retention period, consumer migration window, deprecation interval, or release cadence is promised.

reliances.statement: Turn resolution, bounded source content, and missed-hook activity discovery rely on Conversations' normalized read-only history contract.
Eligible classification and exceptional catch-up rely on Nucleus for bounded agent execution, exact output evidence, and durable requester-tool transport without transferring Decisions authority.
An authorized digest send relies on Email for immediate Resend submission and acceptance reporting; Decisions still owns occurrence and idempotency state and Gmail receipt remains separate.
Continuous observation relies on Codex discovering, trusting, and delivering the installed Stop hook, but no dedicated installed Chancery contract describes that source boundary.
Periodic observer and daily-digest invocation rely on per-user launchd supervision, but no dedicated installed Chancery contract describes launchd readiness.
